english.title: Sale of gunpowder / fireworks to person under 16
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) sold gunpowder to **(..SPECIFY PERSON..) a person apparently under the age of 16 years
english.legislation: Contrary to section 31 of the Explosives Act 1875.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
sell gunpowder to a person under 16 years of age

investigatoraction.description: Guilty Plea by letter procedure may be offered for this offence
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes: Consider the more serious offences of supplying fireworks to persons under 18 (category 2 and 3) or under 16 (category 1 - being caps, cracker snaps, novelty matches, party poppers, serpents and throwdowns) under the Pyrotechnic Articles (Safety) Regulations 2015.
english.standardstatementoffacts: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) the defendant sold gunpowder to **(..SPECIFY PERSON..) a person apparently under the age of 16 years.

other.penalty:
A fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale.

Time limit for prosecutions:
6 months

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
